title: Google DeepMind AlphaEvolve Raises Lower Bounds on Nine Classical Ramsey Numbers
aiSystem: AlphaEvolve (Reinforced Combinatorial Program Search, Google DeepMind)
whyItMatters: Google DeepMind researchers used AlphaEvolve to evolve explicit Ramsey graph constructors that broke decades-old lower bounds on nine classical Ramsey numbers including R(3,13), R(3,18), R(4,13), R(4,14), and R(4,15).
summary: In a working paper posted March 10, 2026 (revised through April 21, 2026, arXiv:2603.09172), Ansh Nagda, Prabhakar Raghavan, and Abhradeep Thakurta at Google DeepMind applied AlphaEvolve to evolve combinatorial search algorithms and structured graph constructions for classical two-color Ramsey numbers R(r, s). Rather than searching raw adjacency matrices directly, AlphaEvolve discovered compact constructive programs that produced explicitly verified clique-free, independent-set-free witness graphs—establishing new record lower bounds for nine classical Ramsey numbers of the form R(3, s) and R(4, s) tracked in Radziszowski’s canonical Dynamic Survey.
technicalHighlights: Improved lower bounds on nine classical two-color Ramsey numbers (initially five—R(3,13), R(3,18), R(4,13), R(4,14), R(4,15)—expanded to nine in v5).
Every new bound is backed by an explicit finite witness graph independently verifiable by exact clique-checking algorithms.
Demonstrated evolutionary program search outperforming decades of bespoke human algebraic and computational Ramsey constructions.
caveats: Improves finite constructive lower bounds rather than asymptotic Ramsey growth exponents; witness graphs remain verified computationally while exact Ramsey values remain open.

scoreRationale.foundational: Moving even a single classical Ramsey number lower bound in Radziszowski’s canonical table is a major result in extremal combinatorics; raising nine in one stroke is historic.
scoreRationale.ripple: Sparked a wave of 2026 AI-assisted Ramsey witness searches (e.g., R(6,8), R(8,10), R(3,33)) across combinatorics.
scoreRationale.verification: Backed by explicit, deterministically checkable finite graph witnesses verified against exact clique/independent-set checkers.
scoreRationale.velocity: Evolved high-performing graph-construction heuristics automatically across a super-exponential combinatorial search space.
